canonical_seed.student_text: An air-hockey puck is already moving straight across a nearly frictionless table. If the net force on it is zero, what does Newton’s First Law predict?
canonical_seed.student_html:
An air-hockey puck is already moving straight across a nearly frictionless table. If the net force on it is zero, what does Newton’s First Law predict?

  1. It must gradually stop because motion always requires a forward net force.
  2. A force called inertia keeps pushing it in its current direction.
  3. Zero net force means no individual forces can be acting.
  4. Its state of motion remains unchanged unless a nonzero net force acts.

choices.text: It must gradually stop because motion always requires a forward net force.
A force called inertia keeps pushing it in its current direction.
Zero net force means no individual forces can be acting.
Its state of motion remains unchanged unless a nonzero net force acts.

canonical_seed.answer: Its state of motion remains unchanged unless a nonzero net force acts.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Newton’s First Law says zero net force means no acceleration: rest remains rest, and constant straight-line velocity remains unchanged.

  3. If an object is not accelerating, only its weight can act.
  4. Support force is another name for inertia.

choices.text: Forces can act and still add to zero net force; for example, tension upward and weight downward.
Zero net force means every individual force has disappeared.
If an object is not accelerating, only its weight can act.
Support force is another name for inertia.
